rationale: Retain the existing canonical American Student Transportation Partners (ASTP) company and retire the unparenthesized seed-only duplicate. Direct company and transaction-party sources establish both names as one platform. Access Holdings described the sale to CVC DIF as a successful exit by September 15, 2025, so the acquisition is closed and one CVC DIF ownership period through DIF Infrastructure VII remains active. Krise and Assisted are operating companies and the Brandywine routes are acquired assets beneath ASTP.

companyFieldUpdates.description: American Student Transportation Partners (ASTP) provides contracted K-12 student transportation through traditional school-bus routes and alternative and special-needs transportation. It serves school districts through route-based operations supported by vehicles, depots, drivers and local operating systems. At the August 2025 transaction announcement, ASTP transported more than 90,000 students annually for more than 50 districts with more than 2,300 vehicles. CVC DIF agreed to acquire the platform from Access Holdings through DIF Infrastructure VII on August 12, 2025, and Access described the sale as a successful exit by September 15, 2025. The exact legal close date, stake and acquisition vehicle below the fund are not publicly disclosed. Krise Transportation and Assisted Student Transportation are operating companies beneath ASTP, and Brandywine routes and vehicles are acquired assets rather than separate manager-level PortCos. No later platform sale or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.

set.event: American Student Transportation Partners was established after Access Holdings acquired Krise Transportation.
ASTP acquired Assisted Transportation Services, expanding its alternative student-transportation operations in the Midwest.
ASTP acquired more than 300 Brandywine routes and vehicles and integrated them into Krise Transportation.
CVC DIF agreed to acquire ASTP from Access Holdings through DIF Infrastructure VII.
Access Holdings described ASTP's sale to CVC DIF as a successful exit, confirming the transaction had completed by that date.
ASTP continued operating through Krise and Assisted across Pennsylvania, Kansas and Missouri.
CVC DIF reported that ASTP served more than 90,000 students annually across more than 50 districts with more than 2,300 vehicles.
Access Holdings completed its exit from ASTP to CVC DIF; the exact legal closing date was not publicly disclosed.
